findings.title: Rate bucket key drops userId, collapsing per-user limits into one shared per-route bucket

steps.to: bucket key derived from base contract (src/bucket.ts:2 @ 5555555555555555555555555555555555555555)
steps.relationship: the change replaces the user-scoped `${userId}:${route}` key with a route-only key, so the returned key no longer varies by userId

impactPath.limitation: Callers of rateBucket are not included in the supplied context; downstream rate-limit enforcement behavior is inferred from the function name and parameter list.

findings.behavioralContract: A rate-limit bucket key for (userId, route) must depend on userId so each user's requests are counted against that user's own bucket.
findings.failureScenario: After deploy, every user maps to the same key for a route. User A sends traffic until the shared bucket is exhausted; users B..N are then rejected on that route despite never exceeding their own quotas, or per-user quota enforcement silently becomes a single global quota.
findings.reachability: Every call to rateBucket on head returns a userId-independent value, so any caller using the return value as a limiter key reaches the shared-bucket behavior on the first request after this change lands.
findings.rootCause: Head replaces the `${userId}:${route}` key with `route`, dropping the user dimension from the bucket key while leaving the now-unused userId parameter in the signature.
findings.impact: Per-user rate limiting collapses to a single shared per-route bucket: one user's consumption counts against all users, enabling exhaustion of the route's quota (denial of service for other users) and removing per-user fairness and quota enforcement.
findings.blastRadius: All callers that use rateBucket's return value as a rate-limit key, and all users of the routes limited through it.
assumptions: Callers use rateBucket's return value as a rate-limiting bucket key, as the function name and parameters indicate.
The change is not a deliberate move to a global per-route limit; if it were, the now-unused userId parameter would typically have been removed.
counterEvidence: The change could be an intentional switch to a global per-route bucket; no caller code was supplied to confirm either way.
No test or configuration in the supplied context contradicts the per-user contract implied by the signature.
findings.uncertainty: Caller usage is inferred from the function name and signature; the supplied context contains no callers, so downstream enforcement impact could not be directly verified.
findings.fix: Restore the user-scoped key: return `${userId}:${route}`. If a global per-route limit is actually intended, remove the userId parameter from the signature and update callers deliberately, including a migration for any bucket state persisted under the old key format.
findings.regressionTest: Add a unit test asserting rateBucket('userA', '/x') !== rateBucket('userB', '/x'); before the fix both return '/x' and the assertion fails, after restoring the template it passes.

groups.rootCause: Head replaces the `${userId}:${route}` key with `route`, dropping the user dimension from the bucket key while leaving the now-unused userId parameter in the signature.

supportingEvidence.evidence: export function rateBucket(userId: string, route: string): string {

findings.title: Rate-limit bucket key drops userId, collapsing per-user buckets into one shared per-route bucket

steps.from: rateBucket returns a route-only key (head line 2)
steps.to: gateway.throttle returns rateBucket(userId, route) as its result
steps.relationship: return value propagates to the caller as the bucket identity

impactPath.limitation: The downstream storage/lookup that consumes the bucket key is outside the supplied indexed context; the enforcement point is inferred from the rateBucket/throttle naming and key semantics.

findings.behavioralContract: rateBucket(userId, route) must yield a key that isolates rate-limit accounting per user and route; the userId parameter must influence the key.
findings.failureScenario: User A generates traffic up to the route's budget; because head keys the bucket by route alone, A's consumption exhausts the single shared bucket for that route and user B's legitimate requests are throttled, while abusive activity is no longer contained to the abuser's own bucket.
findings.reachability: Every invocation of rateBucket executes the changed return; the supplied caller gateway.throttle (src/gateway.ts:3) passes userId and receives the shared key on every throttled request.
findings.rootCause: The head change replaces the `${userId}:${route}` key with `route`, dropping user scoping while leaving userId unused in the signature.
findings.impact: All users of a route share one rate-limit bucket: per-user isolation is lost and a single user's consumption can throttle all others on that route (denial-of-service amplification).
findings.blastRadius: All callers of rateBucket (including gateway.throttle) and all users of every throttled route; per-user rate-limit accounting wherever this key is used.
assumptions: The returned string is used as a rate-limit bucket identifier, consistent with the function and caller names.
No caller relies on the new route-only key semantics.
counterEvidence: The change could be an intentional switch to a global per-route limit, but the retained unused userId parameter and the unchanged gateway.throttle call site provide no supporting evidence for that intent.
Only one caller is visible in the bounded context; other callers with different expectations cannot be ruled out.
findings.uncertainty: Whether the route-only key is an intentional switch to global throttling cannot be confirmed from the supplied diff and single-caller context.
findings.fix: Restore user scoping in the key: return `${userId}:${route}`;. If a global per-route bucket is genuinely intended, explicitly re-signature the function (drop userId), update all call sites, and document the new semantics.
findings.regressionTest: Add a unit test asserting distinct keys per user for the same route: expect(rateBucket('alice','/api')).not.toBe(rateBucket('bob','/api')); it fails on head (both return '/api') and passes after the fix.
